title: Water Heater Rebates in Toronto 2026: $500, With Strings
desc: Toronto heat pump water heater rebate for 2026: $500 under Home Renovation Savings, but only with an assessment and a second upgrade, and not for condo tanks.
lead: Toronto's heat pump water heater rebate is $500, and it is not available on its own. With 47% of households in tall apartments, many Toronto owners are also not eligible at all.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump water heater in Toronto
cards_intro: We re-read the program's page and its eligibility requirements on October 3, 2026. There is no stand-alone water heater rebate in Ontario's program. The $500 comes with an assessment and at least one other upgrade.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Paid for replacing a gas, oil, propane or electric water heater with an ENERGY STAR certified heat pump water heater on NRCan's list, installed by a licensed professional.

cards.title: Not a stand-alone rebate
cards.note: The $500 is only paid inside the assessment stream, which requires at least two qualified measures. A water heater counts as one.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: $600 comes back when the program is completed. The first and follow-up assessments cost money up front, and $600 comes back when the program is completed.

cards.title: Three or more upgrades
cards.note: A third qualified upgrade, such as insulation, windows or air sealing, earns another $500.

cards.title: Program cap
cards.note: $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood and $5,000 for Enbridge gas homes, across all measures.

cards.title: Toronto HELP loan
cards.note: A City loan for energy upgrades. Current rates were not re-verified.

after_cards: The post-audit must be scheduled by November 30, 2026 and completed by December 31, 2026, or within 180 days of your first assessment, whichever comes first.
sections: Some older Toronto pages suggested a condo owner with an in-suite tank might qualify. The program's rules say otherwise: the stream is for single detached, semi-detached, row, townhome and mobile homes, and apartments and condos are excluded. About 35% of Toronto's 1,160,895 households live in an eligible house type, and 52% own.
Why it needs a partner upgrade

The assessment stream requires at least two qualified measures, and a heat pump water heater is one. The simplest partner for an older Toronto house is attic insulation, which can pay up to $1,500 and is often the cheapest big upgrade. With two measures done you get $500 plus the insulation rebate, and a third measure adds $500 more.

A Toronto house with an electric tank and a thin attic could receive $500 for the water heater, up to $1,500 for the attic, and $600 back for the two assessments, which is up to $2,600 before the cost of those assessments. That is our arithmetic from the program's tables. About 58% of Toronto households live in homes built before 1981, and 185,275 are owner-occupied detached houses of that age.

NRCan's product list shows a rebate amount next to each heat pump water heater. That amount is from the old Canada Greener Homes Grant, which has closed, not from this program. The program pays $500 whatever the list shows. The unit must still appear on the list and be ENERGY STAR certified.
Toronto's Home Energy Loan Program can cover the contractor while rebates are paid after the post-audit. We have not re-verified the current rate, so check the City's page.

The first assessment is an EnerGuide home energy evaluation done by a registered energy advisor licensed by Natural Resources Canada, working for an authorized service organization. It must happen before any work, and the program recommends using the same advisor for the follow-up. After it you receive a report of recommended upgrades, from which you choose at least two to complete.

At the follow-up assessment the advisor needs the invoices for both assessments and for each upgrade, plus a copy of your property tax bill. Once the advisor has submitted everything, the rebate arrives within 60 days by cheque or within 30 days by Interac e-Transfer. A Toronto owner should choose the payment method early and keep copies of every document.
claim_steps: Confirm that you own a detached, semi, row or townhome, not a condo or apartment.
Book the first home energy assessment with a registered energy advisor before any work starts.
Choose at least one more upgrade to pair with the water heater, such as insulation, windows or air sealing.
Choose an ENERGY STAR certified heat pump water heater from NRCan's list and have a licensed, trained professional install it.
Keep invoices and your property tax bill, and book the follow-up assessment before the December 31, 2026 deadline.
faq: Can a Toronto condo owner claim?
No. Condos and apartments are excluded.
Can I claim the water heater alone?
No. The assessment stream needs two qualified measures.
What does the NRCan list rebate mean?
It is the old Greener Homes amount, from a grant that has closed, not this program's.
